skills.name: parametrize_plane_conics_as_projective_space
skills.description: Identify the set of plane conics with the projective space of homogeneous quadratic forms, giving an explicit isomorphism between the Hilbert scheme of conics in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) and \(\mathbb{P}^5\).
skills.preconditions: A projective plane \(\mathbb{P}^2\) over a field and the desire to describe degree‑2 curves (conics) on it.
skills.postconditions: A bijective correspondence \(\{\text{conics in }\mathbb{P}^2\}\leftrightarrow \mathbb{P}^5\) sending a quadratic form \(Q\) to its class \([Q]\).
skills.example: Over \(\mathbb{C}\), the conic defined by \(x^2+yz=0\) corresponds to the point \([1:0:0:0:1:0]\in\mathbb{P}^5\) where the coordinates are the coefficients of \(x^2, xy, xz, y^2, yz, z^2\).

skills.name: detect_smooth_conic_via_discriminant
skills.description: Use the discriminant of a quadratic form to test whether the associated conic is smooth (non‑singular).
skills.preconditions: A quadratic form \(Q\) representing a conic in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) and the ability to compute its 3×3 symmetric matrix.
skills.postconditions: A Boolean answer: the conic is smooth iff the discriminant (determinant of the matrix) is non‑zero.
skills.example: For \(Q = x^2 + y^2 + z^2\) the associated matrix is the identity, whose determinant is 1 \(\neq 0\); thus the conic is smooth.

skills.name: translate_tangency_condition_to_linear_equation_in_dual_projective_space
skills.description: Express the condition that two conics are tangent at a point as a linear equation in the dual projective space of lines, using the fact that tangency imposes a single linear relation on the coefficients of the second conic once the point and tangent line are fixed.
skills.preconditions: A fixed smooth conic \(C\) and a point \(P\in C\) together with its tangent line \(T_P C\).
skills.postconditions: A linear equation in the coordinates of a second conic \(C'\) that characterises all \(C'\) tangent to \(C\) at \(P\).
skills.example: If \(C\) is given by \(x^2+y^2-z^2=0\) and \(P=[1:0:1]\), the tangent line is \(x-z=0\); any conic \(C'\) tangent to \(C\) at \(P\) must satisfy the linear relation \(a_{xz}+a_{zz}=0\) among its coefficients.

skills.name: compute_intersection_number_using_bezout_theorem
skills.description: Apply Bézout's theorem to compute the total intersection multiplicity of two projective plane curves with no common component, as the product of their degrees.
skills.preconditions: Two projective plane curves \(C_1, C_2\) of degrees \(d_1, d_2\) that share no irreducible component.
skills.postconditions: The sum of intersection multiplicities over all points of \(C_1\cap C_2\) equals \(d_1 d_2\).
skills.example: A line (degree 1) and a cubic (degree 3) intersect in exactly three points counted with multiplicity, because \(1\times 3 = 3\).

skills.name: determine_degree_of_finite_morphism_via_generic_fiber
skills.description: Find the degree of a finite morphism by counting the number of geometric points in a generic fiber, using the fact that the degree is locally constant on a dense open set.
skills.preconditions: A finite morphism \(f: X\to Y\) of varieties and a point \(y\in Y\) lying in the open set where \(f\) is flat.
skills.postconditions: The integer \(\deg f\) equal to \#\(f^{-1}(y)\) (counted with multiplicities) for any such generic \(y\).
skills.example: The map \(\mathbb{A}^1\to\mathbb{A}^1\), \(t\mapsto t^3\), is finite; over a generic value \(a\neq 0\) the fiber has three points, so \(\deg f = 3\).

skills.name: apply_lang_weil_estimate_to_point_counts_over_finite_fields
skills.description: Use the Lang–Weil estimate to relate the number of \(\mathbb{F}_q\)-rational points of a geometrically irreducible variety to its dimension and degree, obtaining an error term of order \(q^{\dim-1/2}\).
skills.preconditions: A geometrically irreducible variety \(X\) of dimension \(d\) and degree \(\delta\) defined over \(\mathbb{F}_q\).
skills.postconditions: An estimate \(|\#X(\mathbb{F}_q) - q^d| \le C\,\delta\, q^{d-1/2}\) for some constant \(C\) depending only on \(d\).
skills.example: For a smooth plane cubic (dimension 1, degree 3) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\), Lang–Weil gives \(|\#E(\mathbb{F}_p) - p| \le 2\sqrt{p}\).

skills.name: relate_average_fiber_size_to_degree_using_etale_covering
skills.description: When a morphism is finite étale over a dense open subset, the average number of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-points in its fibers over that open set converges to the degree of the covering as \(p\to\infty\).
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism \(f: X\to Y\) defined over \(\mathbb{Z}\) and a dense open \(U\subset Y\) where \(f\) is étale.
skills.example: The map \(\mathbb{A}^1\to\mathbb{A}^1\), \(t\mapsto t^2\), is étale away from 0; averaging \#preimages over \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\) gives limit 2, the degree.

skills.name: verify_finite_etale_over_dense_open_using_jacobian_criterion
skills.description: Apply the Jacobian criterion to a morphism of varieties to check that it is smooth and unramified (hence étale) on a dense open subset.
skills.preconditions: A morphism \(f: X\to Y\) defined by polynomial equations, and the ability to compute the Jacobian matrix of the defining equations with respect to the source coordinates.
skills.postconditions: A Zariski open subset \(U\subset Y\) such that \(f^{-1}(U)\to U\) is étale (i.e., the Jacobian has full rank at every point of the preimage).
skills.example: For \(f: \mathbb{A}^2\to\mathbb{A}^1\), \((x,y)\mapsto x^2+y^2\), the Jacobian \((2x,2y)\) has rank 1 except at the origin; thus \(f\) is étale over \(\mathbb{A}^1\setminus\{0\}\).

skills.name: use_monodromy_to_show_geometric_irreducibility_of_fiber
skills.description: Employ the monodromy group of a finite cover to prove that a generic fiber is geometrically irreducible, using transitivity of the action on the fiber.
skills.preconditions: A finite dominant morphism \(f: X\to Y\) with a known monodromy representation of the fundamental group of a Zariski open subset of \(Y\) acting on a generic fiber.
skills.postconditions: Conclusion that the generic fiber is a single geometrically irreducible component because the monodromy action is transitive.
skills.example: For the map \(\mathbb{A}^1\to\mathbb{A}^1\), \(t\mapsto t^n\), the monodromy group is the cyclic group of order \(n\) acting transitively on the \(n\) roots, so the generic fiber consists of \(n\) distinct points (geometrically irreducible as a zero‑dimensional scheme).

skills.name: pass_to_limit_of_point_counts_to_obtain_geometric_degree
skills.description: Combine Lang–Weil estimates with the étale average‑fiber argument to deduce that the limiting average of \(\#f^{-1}(y)\) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-points equals the geometric degree of \(f\).
skills.preconditions: A finite morphism \(f: X\to Y\) that is étale over a dense open \(U\subset Y\) and a Lang–Weil bound for \(U\).
skills.postconditions: A formula \(L = \deg f\) where \(L\) is the limit \(\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#U(\mathbb{F}_p)}\sum_{y\in U(\mathbb{F}_p)} \#f^{-1}(y)\).
skills.example: For the covering \(t\mapsto t^3\) of \(\mathbb{A}^1\) ramified only at 0, applying the limit over \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\) yields \(L=3\), the degree of the map.
